facts.program: BC Hydro heat pump rebate (Home Renovation Rebate)
facts.claim: Whole-home heat pump rebate
facts.amount: up to $4,000
facts.eligibility: Heat pump meets 100% of heating at -5C; must REPLACE electric heat (baseboards/electric furnace); HPCN member installer; model on eligible list (variable speed, AHRI ref, HSPF2 >= 8.5, SEER2 >= 15.2)
facts.notes: Gas/oil/propane-heated homes get nothing from this rebate unless income-qualified (see ESP).

facts.claim: Partial heat pump rebate
facts.eligibility: Heat pump meets at least 50% of heating; replacing electric heat; HPCN installer

facts.claim: Limited-time bonus
facts.amount: up to $1,000
facts.eligibility: Installs completed, invoiced and paid Aug 1 - Oct 31, 2026; apply by Nov 30, 2026; also entry into a draw for three $5,000 prizes

facts.claim: Gas/propane/oil to central ducted or 3+ head heat pump
facts.eligibility: Income-qualified household (limits by household size), assessed value <= $1.2M (L1/L2) or $1.82M (L3), pre-registration before work, ESP Registered Contractor
facts.notes: 2-head/2 mini-split: $11,000/$5,500/$1,000; single-head mini-split: $5,500/$4,500/$1,000 (gas). 2026-10-09: Better Homes BC ESP program page re-read (heat pump max $13,000, income table); the July 6 requirements PDF itself could not be opened in the browser, so per-level amounts still rest on the 2026-09-26 read.

facts.claim: Extra for northern homes
facts.amount: +$3,000 (central/multi-split/2 mini-splits) or +$1,500 (single-head), Level 1 and 2 only
facts.eligibility: At or north of 100 Mile House (51.628N) AND BC Hydro electric service. Prince George and Fort St. John qualify.
facts.notes: The only path to $16,000 is Level 1 + northern top-up ($13,000 + $3,000) on a fossil-fuel home.

facts.program: CleanBC ESP electric to heat pump
facts.claim: Electric-heated home to heat pump
facts.amount: up to $5,000
facts.eligibility: Income Level 1 only
facts.notes: 2026-10-09: Better Homes BC ESP program page re-read (heat pump max $13,000, income table); the July 6 requirements PDF itself could not be opened in the browser, so per-level amounts still rest on the 2026-09-26 read.

facts.claim: Household of 4 limits
facts.notes: ESP accepts BC Hydro, FortisBC Inc., FortisBC gas, City of Penticton, New Westminster, Grand Forks, Nelson Hydro, Summerland, PNG accounts.

facts.claim: Heat pump water heater (from fossil fuel); electrical service upgrade; HRV/ERV
facts.amount: HPWH up to $3,500 (L1-L3, from fossil); electrical service upgrade $5,000/$3,500/$1,500; ventilation HRV/ERV up to $1,600 or fan $300 (L1-L2)
facts.eligibility: Income-qualified; electrical service upgrade only when switching fossil fuel to heat pump
facts.notes: ESP 2026 requirements contain no insulation or window rebates.

facts.claim: Insulation
facts.amount: up to $5,500 total; attic $0.02 x R x sqft max $900; basement/crawlspace, wall cavity, wall sheathing $0.09 x R x sqft max $1,200 each; other $0.07 max $1,000
facts.eligibility: Electrically heated homes, BC Hydro account, HPCN contractor, minimum R-values

facts.program: BC Hydro windows and doors rebate
facts.claim: Windows/doors
facts.amount: $100 per window or door, max $2,000
facts.eligibility: U-factor <= 1.22 W/m2K, licensed contractor, replacing existing units; homes in City of Vancouver not eligible for Tier 2 window/door rebates

facts.program: BC Hydro heat pump water heater rebate
facts.claim: HPWH
facts.amount: up to $1,000
facts.eligibility: Replacing electric primary water heater; NEEA Tier 2+; licensed contractor
facts.notes: Multiple-upgrade bonus up to $2,000 mentioned on this page.

facts.claim: Solar PV
facts.amount: $1,000/kW DC, max 50% of cost, cap $5,000 residential
facts.eligibility: BC Hydro customer, HPCN member designs/installs
facts.dates: First come, first served while funding lasts
facts.notes: Re-read 2026-10-03: steps list hiring an HPCN member and submitting a self-generation application before installing; payment within 60 days of approval; owners of single-family homes, duplexes, townhomes, mobile homes in BC Hydro territory.

facts.claim: Battery storage
facts.amount: $500/kWh, max 50% of cost; cap $1,500 standard, $5,000 with Peak Saver
facts.eligibility: Qualified product list; battery-only allowed only with Peak Saver enrollment; HPCN installer
facts.notes: Combined solar + battery max $10,000. Re-read 2026-10-03: steps list hiring an HPCN member and submitting a self-generation application before installing; payment within 60 days of approval; owners of single-family homes, duplexes, townhomes, mobile homes in BC Hydro territory.

facts.claim: Home Level 2 charger
facts.amount: 50% of cost up to $350; +$200 for EV power-management device
facts.eligibility: Single-family, row home, duplex (mobile and manufactured homes with a private garage or dedicated parking count as single-family); new Level 2 (208 or 240V) J1772 or NACS J3400 charger on BC Hydro's eligible list, bought not leased from a Canadian supplier, certified for Canada, permanent wall-mounted install in an occupied home; electrical permit; Tesla charging stations no longer eligible
facts.notes: Re-read 2026-10-16. Eligible costs: charger, licensed-electrician labour, permits, electrical design, power management device. Not eligible: the cost of only installing a 240V outlet. Three ways to apply: licensed electrician (invoice, permit number, photo); non-electrician with inspection certificate; existing permitted 240V outlet (charger invoice and photo only). Paid within 90 days of applying. Combined incentives are capped at total cost. FortisBC electricity customers apply through FortisBC.

facts.claim: Device enrollment/seasonal rewards
facts.amount: Thermostat $100/$50; EV charger $250/$50; battery $500/$250; load controller $100/$50; water heater $100/$50
facts.eligibility: Thermostats: line-voltage baseboard only (Mysa, Sinope). Events Nov-Mar, max 4 hours, opt out any time.
facts.notes: Re-read 2026-10-11. Eligible thermostats: Mysa baseboard v2, Gen 3 and LITE; Sinopé baseboard and LITE (no ecobee or Nest). Thermostat enrollment bonus $100 is not paid for free thermostats. Events up to 4 hours, opt out any time; more than 50% opt-outs may forfeit the seasonal reward. Owner, or tenant with the owner's consent. E-Plus rate accounts are not eligible.

facts.claim: Free Mysa/Sinope thermostats
facts.amount: Up to 5 free (valued at $600); $50 seasonal Peak Saver reward
facts.eligibility: Baseboard-heated BC Hydro customers; pre-enrolled in Peak Saver
facts.dates: Ordering open from fall 2026; no end date shown
facts.notes: Re-read 2026-10-11 on BC Hydro's free-smart-thermostats page: ordering is open. Up to five free thermostats, valued at $600. Sinopé fits two-wire setups, Mysa four-wire. Needs a BC Hydro residential account, a MyHydro account, electric baseboard heat, install at the account's service address, and Peak Saver enrollment at checkout. Free thermostats get no Peak Saver enrollment bonus; the $50 seasonal reward is per household, paid as a bill credit after winter, and may be lost if you opt out of more than half the events. Renters need landlord permission. Heat pump homes are not eligible. Installing a hardwired thermostat is regulated electrical work (Technical Safety BC). The page does not mention an income-qualified $100 reward.

facts.claim: Vernon electricity is BC Hydro (gas is FortisBC)
facts.notes: Site had said FortisBC. Wrong.

facts.claim: Penticton electricity is the City of Penticton municipal utility (wholesale supply from FortisBC); City runs HELP loan up to $10,000 over 10 years on the utility bill
facts.notes: BC Hydro rebates do not apply to City of Penticton electric accounts; CleanBC ESP does accept them.

facts.claim: Kelowna electricity is FortisBC (FortisBC substations serve downtown and south-central Kelowna)
facts.notes: Some fringe areas may differ; homeowners should check the name on their power bill. BC Hydro rebates do not apply to FortisBC electric accounts.

facts.claim: All other BC cities in slice (Abbotsford, Burnaby, Chilliwack, Coquitlam, Fort St. John, Kamloops, Langley, Maple Ridge, Nanaimo, Prince George, Richmond, Squamish, Surrey, Vancouver, Victoria) are BC Hydro electric
facts.notes: Hub pages had been overwritten (commit 71d7a3c24) with Kelowna's FortisBC text for 14 cities.

facts.program: BC Hydro Home Renovation Rebate eligibility
facts.claim: Who can apply
facts.amount: n/a
facts.eligibility: Home primarily heated by electricity (heating system able to heat at least 50% of the home to 22C); BC Hydro account or municipal utility in BC Hydro territory; account holder applies or signs consent form; home 12 months or older; single-detached (with suite), fixed mobile home, duplex, row home or townhouse with own meters (not a strata-held account), small multiplex; not condo or apartment buildings; heat pump and insulation need an HPCN member; income-qualified customers should use CleanBC Better Homes ESP instead (cannot combine); rebate cannot exceed invoice cost

facts.program: CleanBC Energy Savings Program (ESP) income limits
facts.claim: Maximum household income for Level 1, 2 and 3 rebates, by household size
facts.eligibility: Combined pre-tax income of all adults in the home, excluding dependents; also depends on assessed property value. Level 3 is only for ground-oriented homes switching from natural gas, propane or oil to an electric heat pump. Year-round primary residence at least 12 months old; account with BC Hydro, FortisBC or a municipal utility; renters need a landlord consent form.
facts.notes: Page banner on 2026-10-09 says the site is not being updated during the provincial election period except for health and safety or statutory topics. Re-check at the monthly run.

facts.program: BC Hydro Home Renovation multi-upgrade bonus
facts.claim: Bonus rebate for completing more than one upgrade
facts.amount: up to $2,000
facts.eligibility: Complete more than one upgrade under the Home Renovation Rebate Program (a partnership of the Province, BC Hydro and FortisBC). Conditions are on BC Hydro's terms and conditions PDFs, which were not opened.
facts.dates: No end date shown on the heat pump page
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-09. The heat pump bonus page also lists a draw for three $5,000 prizes for installs paid Aug 1 to Oct 31, 2026.

facts.claim: Extra incentives for customers in select postal codes of: Abbotsford; Campbell Heights neighbourhood in Surrey; select communities between Kelowna and Vernon; Northeast Fraser Valley (Mission to Agassiz); Maple Ridge; Mount Lehman; select neighbourhoods in Victoria; select neighbourhoods in Vancouver west of Cambie; Port Coquitlam, Burke Mountain; Sun Peaks; Vernon; West Kelowna; White Rock. Postal code checker on the page.
facts.amount: Appliance top-up 100% of the regular BC Hydro appliance rebate; heat pump top-up $4,000 whole home / $1,500 partial (total up to $9,000 with the standard rebate and the promotional bonus to Oct 31, 2026); EV charger top-up $1,750 (up to 100% of cost) on top of $350, with $250 Peak Saver bonus, total $2,350
facts.eligibility: Postal code (EV charger: a qualifying feeder) in an eligible area. Appliance top-up only by post-purchase application (app.bchydro.com/estar). Heat pump top-up added automatically by postal code of the install address; HPCN contractor; standard home renovation eligibility.
facts.dates: EV charger top-up: applications Aug 4 to Dec 31, 2026. Appliance top-up follows the current appliance offer (Oct 2, 2026 to Jan 8, 2027). Heat pump promotional bonus to Oct 31, 2026.
facts.notes: Only select postal codes inside these places qualify, not whole cities. Re-read 2026-10-11 with the Top-up details panel open: it shows only the heat pump table (standard up to $4,000; top-up $4,000 whole home / $1,500 partial; promotional bonus $1,000 / $500 to Oct 31, 2026; total up to $9,000). The headline says the top-up is 'up to $8,000, plus an additional bonus up to $1,000' for heat pumps and heat pump water heaters, but no heat pump water heater top-up amount is published there or on BC Hydro's heat pump water heater page, so do not state one. BC Hydro writes 'Port Coquitlam, Burke Mountain'; Burke Mountain is in the City of Coquitlam.

facts.program: BC Hydro Home Renovation Rebate Program upgrade list
facts.claim: Current upgrades: windows and doors (up to $2,000), heat pumps (up to $4,000), insulation (up to $5,500), heat pump water heaters (up to $1,000). No ventilation, HRV or ERV measure. Not available in condo or apartment units.
facts.amount: No HRV/ERV rebate
facts.eligibility: Homes primarily heated by electricity

facts.claim: Rebate on a new eligible connected thermostat for an electric central heating system (electric furnace, electric boiler, combination system or air source heat pump), installed by a licensed contractor when the heating system is installed or serviced
facts.amount: Up to $150; income-qualified up to $200
facts.eligibility: Residential FortisBC electricity account or municipal electricity account of Grand Forks, Penticton, Summerland or Nelson Hydro. Single-family, duplex, triplex, row home, townhouse or mobile home on a permanent foundation, at least 12 months old (income-qualified: 10 years, max 3,500 sq ft). One per home. Not for baseboard heating. No self-installs. Apply within six months of the invoice.
facts.notes: Income-qualified version: https://www.fortisbc.com/rebates/detail/connected-thermostat-rebates-income-qualified (income limits same as ESP Level 1). Thermostats are not bonus-eligible.

facts.program: FortisBC instant rebates on energy-efficient products
facts.claim: Instant in-store rebates at participating retailers: connected baseboard thermostats up to $40 each (limit 5, FortisBC electricity customers only); ENERGY STAR connected thermostats up to $100 (limit 1). In-store only except Mysa.
facts.amount: Up to $40 per baseboard thermostat (5); up to $100 for one ENERGY STAR connected thermostat
facts.eligibility: FortisBC residential electricity customer or municipal electricity customer of Grand Forks, Penticton, Summerland or Nelson Hydro (baseboard thermostat offer: FortisBC electricity customers only)
facts.notes: Offers vary by retailer. Re-check after Oct 31, 2026: set status closed if not renewed.

facts.program: FortisBC clothes washer and dryer rebates
facts.claim: ENERGY STAR clothes washers (IMEF 2.92+, IWF 3.2 or less) and dryers on FortisBC's qualifying lists
facts.amount: Washer $100; dryer $100 (CEF 3.93 to 4.3, or ENERGY STAR gas), $150 (CEF 4.4 to 5.6 or compact), $250 (CEF 5.7+)
facts.eligibility: FortisBC residential electricity customer or municipal electricity customer of Grand Forks, Penticton, Summerland or Nelson Hydro. Up to two rebates per appliance type per household. Apply within 60 days of purchase or delivery.
facts.notes: FortisBC customers get a bill credit; municipal utility customers (Penticton) get a cheque. Up to 90 days to process.

facts.claim: ENERGY STAR fridges, 11 cu ft or more, two or more doors (one fridge, one freezer), on the qualifying list
facts.amount: $50 (10% better than federal standard); $100 (15% better)
facts.eligibility: FortisBC residential electricity customer or municipal electricity customer of Grand Forks, Penticton, Summerland or Nelson Hydro. Up to two per household. Apply within 60 days.

facts.claim: ENERGY STAR bathroom fan system ducted outside, installed with a rebate-eligible insulation, window or door upgrade; not an HRV or ERV
facts.amount: Up to $1,200 per system, maximum $2,400 per home (2 systems)
facts.eligibility: Income-qualified (household income limits equal to ESP Level 1) FortisBC or municipal (Grand Forks, Penticton, Summerland, Nelson) electricity customers whose primary heat is that electricity; owner listed on the account and owning one BC property; home at least 10 years old, max 3,500 sq ft, ground-oriented. Licensed contractor. Cannot be combined with other provincial or federal rebate programs. Apply within six months.
facts.notes: Fans 85 cfm+ at 50 Pa, continuous duty, backdraft damper. Not bonus-eligible.

facts.program: BC Hydro EV power management device rebate
facts.claim: Extra rebate for an EV power management device installed with a Level 2 home charger; the device can avoid an electrical service upgrade (branch circuit sharing, e.g. with a dryer, or feeder monitoring of the whole home)
facts.eligibility: BC Hydro customer in a detached home, row home, duplex or mobile home; eligible device (BC Hydro list) and eligible Level 2 charger; electrical permit; device and charger installed on or after December 1, 2023 (no retroactive installs)
facts.notes: No separate application: added to the home charger rebate. BC Hydro says most homes do not need a device; it is only needed when a service upgrade would otherwise be required. Electrician should review 12 months of meter data to find spare capacity.

facts.claim: Top-ups added to the provincial charger rebate for single-family homes: BC Hydro community-based offers (select postal codes), Regional District of Nanaimo (separate application), BC Hydro power management devices, Indigenous Peoples, City of Kamloops, Resort Municipality of Whistler, District of Squamish
facts.amount: With a local government top-up: up to 75% of purchase and installation costs or the listed dollar amount, whichever is less
facts.eligibility: Added automatically when you apply for the provincial charger rebate, except the Regional District of Nanaimo; first come, first served
facts.notes: Multi-unit top-ups: Kamloops, Saanich, Squamish, Indigenous Peoples, Whistler. Workplace: Indigenous Peoples, Whistler. No Burnaby, Vancouver or Surrey city top-up listed on 2026-10-16.

facts.program: BC EV charger rebates for multi-unit buildings and workplaces
facts.claim: Base provincial rebates for apartment, condo and townhome complexes and for workplaces
facts.amount: Multi-unit: 75% up to $3,000 for an EV ready plan; 50% up to $2,000 per charger; up to $137,000 total for EV Ready building projects (varies by stage). Workplaces: 50% up to $2,000 per charger
facts.eligibility: Buildings built before municipal bylaws required EV ready stalls; program maximums apply
facts.notes: Amounts read from the base-rebate table on the top-ups page.

facts.program: FortisBC home EV charger rebate (CleanBC Go Electric)
facts.claim: Home Level 2 charger rebate for FortisBC electricity customers and municipal utility customers of Grand Forks, Penticton, Summerland and Nelson Hydro
facts.amount: 50% of eligible purchase and installation costs, up to $350
facts.eligibility: Owner, or tenant with landlord consent; single-family detached, mobile home on a permanent foundation, duplexes, triplexes and fourplexes, side-by-side row homes with their own meters and garages, with off-street dedicated parking; townhome, condo and apartment residents use the multi-unit rebates; Tesla-made stations not eligible; Level 2 J1772 or NACS J3400, new, bought not leased in Canada
facts.notes: Taxes, subscriptions and non-EV wiring are not eligible costs. Non-electrician installs need a Technical Safety BC or municipal inspection certificate.

facts.claim: BC Hydro's residential rebate list (renovations: windows and doors, insulation, heat pumps, water heating; products: appliances and air fryers; solar and battery; EV chargers; income-based free programs; Peak Saver; condo units; remote communities) has no residential lighting rebate and no stand-alone electrical service upgrade rebate
facts.notes: Service upgrades are funded only by CleanBC ESP (income-qualified, fossil fuel to heat pump; facts bc-pages-7, bc-blog-21). BC Hydro's $200 EV power management device rebate is the alternative to a service upgrade for EV charging (bc-pages-39). Commercial lighting is a business program, outside this site.

facts.program: Better Homes BC: program-qualified energy advisors
facts.claim: Better Homes BC lists energy advisors who are registered with Natural Resources Canada and have also completed B.C. rebate program training. An EnerGuide evaluation tests a home's airtightness and models its energy use, and some Home Renovation Rebate add-on rebates require one. The advisors are independent businesses, and Better Homes BC tells homeowners to interview and choose their own. Energy coaches answer program questions at 1-844-881-9790.
facts.amount: No amount
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-20 in the browser. The page does not say how its directory search works or when to book, so we state neither.

facts.claim: A grant toward an overdue BC Hydro balance for residential customers facing disconnection after a temporary financial crisis such as job or benefit loss, unexpected medical costs or a death in the family. Maximum grants are $800 for electrically heated homes and $700 for non-electrically heated homes; the grant is equal to the overdue balance up to that maximum. One grant per account holder each year.
facts.amount: Up to $800 electric heat, $700 other heat
facts.eligibility: Residential account holder, primary residence, payments overdue by at least 21 days or facing disconnection, a life event in the last 12 months that caused a temporary crisis, outstanding balance of $1,000 or less, and some attempt to make payments.
facts.notes: Another BC Hydro bill help page was reported by a search summary as still saying $600; we did not read it. The Customer Crisis Fund page itself says $800 and $700. The BC Climate Action Tax Credit amounts were not read on a CRA page, so are not stated.
